messages:
lisa (customer): Hey team — hitting a repeatable issue where SSE stops mid-stream after a network switch. We only get ~120 tokens then the client shows a generic connection closed. Request id r-9f2b7c
ashwin (support): Sorry about that — can you paste the client log around the disconnect and the request id? Any repro steps?
lisa (customer): Repro steps: iPhone 14, iOS 16, app opens stream -> start generation -> enable personal hotspot on another device (wifi->cell handoff) -> stream halts. Client log: `EventSource encountered an error` then `network changed, closing`
Client snippet:
```
EventSource: open
EventSource: message {data: "...partial chunk..."}
EventSource: error (networkerror)
EventSource: close
app: detected interface change: en0 -> pdp_ip0
socket: TLS handshake aborted
```
Headers we sent: `Authorization: Bearer sk-live-REDACTED`, `x-request-id: r-9f2b7c`, `x-region: us-west-2`
devon (eng-runtime): Thanks, that log helps. Two quick things to check: are you reusing the same auth token across reconnects, and do you see a 401 on the server for that x-request-id? If the reconnect happens after token expiry we can see resume attempts fail.
lisa (customer): I can see server-side entries: `r-9f2b7c` had a 200 start, then a `401` about ~3s after the client closed, and then `connection reset` on our side. Token TTL is 300s. No client-side refresh was attempted — app doesn't refresh mid-stream.
devon (eng-runtime): That 401 during resume is the smoking gun. When the client reopens the SSE connection during a network flip it may present the original token; if the token rotation or short-lived session policy invalidates that token during the handoff we reject the resume. Two options: (1) client re-auths and opens a fresh stream (recommended), or (2) server accepts resume attempts up to a short leeway window for the same x-request-id. Also check TCP-level resets from the NAT/handoff (we've seen TLS renegotiation failures cause chunk duplication/loss).
ashwin (support): Quick mitigation: can you try the canary build we pushed that auto-reopens on networkchange and includes a 401 handler to refresh token and immediately re-open? It also retries resume with `?resume_from=last_event_id`.
lisa (customer): Trying canary now — will test back-to-back toggles a few times.
ops-oncall: Logged INC-3456, tagging eng-runtime, setting priority P2 until we confirm mitigation.
monitor-bot: Alert suppressed for r-9f2b7c during verification window.
devon (eng-runtime): Long-term we should add a small resume window: accept identical resumes within 10s and support idempotent resume tokens so clients can reconnect without losing partial output. Also improving heartbeat frequency from 30s -> 15s helps detect broken NATs earlier.
lisa (customer): Canary results: 4/5 runs completed full stream after the client refresh+reopen change. One run still dropped (looks like abrupt carrier NAT reset). Will keep testing. Thanks for the fast turnaround :thumbsup:
nashwin (support): Great — we'll keep INC-3456 open and follow up with a config change for the resume window and a note in the SDK docs about recommended client reconnect behavior (refresh token on 401, exponential backoff, resume param).
file_note: stream-interrupt reconnection pattern: client-side network handoff causing resume 401 and partial outputs — contains repro steps and logs
